items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: Johnny Griffin recorded one of my tunes

ctx.x: Yeah. Tell me about your composing if you would. When did you start writing?

Well you know I was always encouraged to compose. I showed an interest in it with everybody I ever worked with. For most of my jazz life I had to read music and stuff like that, but they were other people’s compositions. And the first person who encouraged me to write music actually was Mike Nock. Because I always played this recorder. It was an instrument I was introduced to when I was 16. But I played mostly bebop and I would compose tunes and Mike Nock liked one of the tunes. Does a tune usually start with the recorder?
